messages:
jaya (acme): Hey team — onboarding BYOK for AcmeCorp. We rotated the AWS CMK last night and now calls to Redwood that need to unwrap customer envelopes fail with 403 or 'unwrap failed: key version mismatch'. We also have Azure Key Vault in staging. Can you help triage?
sofia (support): Sorry you're hitting this, @jaya. Mind pasting one failing request id and the error you see from the Redwood API? Also confirm if the ciphertext blob is customer-provided or generated by Redwood.
jaya (acme): Request id: rq_0a9f3b. Error from API: `unwrap error: kms:DecryptDeniedByPolicy key version mismatch`
So the envelope was generated by our service, then we rotated the CMK in AWS. The ciphertext has been sitting in S3. We suspected rotation would be fine but looks like Redwood fails to unwrap. Ciphertext header (redacted): ```{"alg":"RSA-OAEP","key":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234:1"}```
ev an (solutions): Two quick checks: 1) Is Redwood configured to call the specific key-version ARN (with the :1 suffix) or the key id without version? If the envelope stores a versioned key ARN and the service principal doesn't have Decrypt on that alias/version, KMS will deny. 2) Can you share CloudTrail entry for the failing decrypt? looks for kms:Decrypt with the exact key version in the event.
jaya (acme): here's a CloudTrail-ish snippet (redacted): ```{ "eventName": "Decrypt", "errorMessage": "Access denied", "requestParameters": { "keyId": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234:1" }, "userIdentity": { "arn": "arn:aws:sts::444455556666:assumed-role/redwood-integration/instance" } }```
mike (security): :eyes: That request identity shows Redwood's integration role. Make sure the key policy permits that principal to Decrypt on both the alias and specific key version. AWS KMS can have explicit denies that reference key version ARNs. Also check that there was not a deny added as part of rotation pipeline.
rotation-bot: AWS KMS scheduled rotation executed for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234 at 2025-09-03T23:10:12Z. New key version suffix :2 created and enabled.
audit-bot: CloudTrail: ReEncrypt and GenerateDataKey operations observed around rotation window for key abcd-1234.
sofia (support): Possible root cause: envelope includes a versioned key ARN ("...:1"). After rotation the active material moved to :2 and your stored ciphertext references :1; if the key policy is narrowly scoped to the alias (no version) Redwood should still be able to decrypt, but many customers' IaC pins a version or adds explicit denies. Two mitigations: 1) rewrap the ciphertext to the new key (safe but requires processing all stored blobs), 2) grant Redwood's SP Decrypt permission on the specific old key version (if that's acceptable).
ev an (solutions): For rewrap a simple AWS CLI flow: ```aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://cipher.blob --source-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234:1 --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/abcd-1234:2 --output text > cipher_v2.blob``` That re-encrypts to the new key material. We can help script a batch rewrap for S3 objects.
jaya (acme): For Azure staging we saw similar: app failed with `Unauthorized` on `unwrapKey`. How should we grant access?
sofia (support): For Azure Key Vault the Redwood service principal needs Key Permissions: `wrapKey`, `unwrapKey`, and `get` on the key. Example Azure CLI: ```az keyvault set-policy -n myVault --spn <REDWOOD-SPN> --key-permissions wrapKey unwrapKey get``` Also double-check RBAC vs access-policy model depending on your vault configuration.
mike (security): One more note re: vulnerability triage — there was a low-severity CVE in kms-client v1.2.3 that impacted legacy key parsing, but it's not likely related to this error. Still worth verifying the runtime libs on any sidecar rewrap tooling.
sofia (support): Short-term plan: I can coordinate a minimal rewrap job for the batch of affected objects, or you can add the Decrypt permission on the old key version to avoid rewrap. We'll need a confirmation that policy change is allowed by your security/compliance team.
jaya (acme): Compliance prefers not to widen old key permissions. Let's proceed with a rewrap. Can Redwood run that?
ev an (solutions): Yes — we can run a one-time rewrap. We'll need S3 bucket prefix, role to access objects, and estimated object count. We'll create a scoped runbook and provide a dry-run.
sofia (support): Filing internal doc ticket to add a KB on multi-kms rotations and fallback behavior — DOCS-1427. We'll also add guidance to not pin key-version ARNs in envelope headers.
mike (security): I'll audit CloudTrail to confirm no anomalous denies during rotation and sign off once rewrap is done.
jaya (acme): Thanks all :thumbsup: Appreciate the help. Please DM next steps and the runbook.
sofia (support): Will DM you the runbook and schedule a short handoff. Marking this thread as action: rewrap job + docs ticket. :white_check_mark:
